core_question: Is the remaining shortfall in native-gap closure a matter of measurement noise (trial reliability), or a representational ceiling of a single outside axis on the zero-target base (e.g., a second dimension or a within-support component is needed)?
rationale: Outside axis estimable from few repeats (E_AXIS Holm-significant at every T; ARF>=0.50 by T=2; fidelity 0.33->1.0; trial-8 axis == sealed axis exactly). But TOTAL_RECOVERY_ZERO_BASE reaches only ~0.41-0.44 at T=4 and ~0.50/0.58 at full resource -> the D=1 + zero-target-base ceiling sits near the 0.50 bar; T_AXIS_STAR NOT_ESTABLISHED_BY_T4 in both primary ROIs.
